## From the case studies to the whole model

The case studies use a narrow slice of DSSAT. The [Java rice case study](../java/index.qmd), for one, runs one crop
model, two water regimes, one cultivar and a calibration of a single soil fertility factor. DSSAT does far more: 
its engine carries cultivar files for 48 crop codes (59 files in the engine's `Genotype` folder), and it simulates 
phenology and growth, the water and nitrogen balance of the soil, the effect of management, and
seasons, risks and rotations over many years. The bridge that xdssat builds between DSSAT and Python is just as
useful for exploring all of that. The modules below do it with the course material of a DSSAT training, one
module per training day, every exercise rebuilt in Python on top of xdssat's modules.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Based on the DSSAT training in Chiang Mai, 2018.**    
The following material is based on the DSSAT
training I attended in Chiang Mai, Thailand, in 2018. The trainers were
[Prof. Gerrit Hoogenboom](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=6t7Zm4oAAAAJ) from the University
of Florida, USA, and [Prof. Attachai Jintrawet](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=HHRpPm4AAAAJ)
from Chiang Mai University.
:::

The training ran from 27 August to 1 September 2018, as described in my
[blog post about it](https://benny.istan.to/blog/20180911-dssat-training-in-chiang-mai-2018.html). The
modules follow its day-by-day syllabus and its exercises. They are written for this site: the course's slides
and exercise sheets are not reproduced. Where the course handed out data files for an exercise, the notebooks use
them (they are in `docs/notebooks/course-data/`); everything else comes from DSSAT's openly published example
data, [DSSAT/dssat-csm-data](https://github.com/DSSAT/dssat-csm-data). Two parts of the syllabus are handled
differently: day 5's demonstration of a spatial decision support tool (MWCropDSS) is replaced by the sections
"From one field to a grid: xdssat" at the end of modules 1, 2, 3 and 5, and day 6, for which no course material
is used here, follows DSSAT's own sequence examples and documentation (module 6). The course worked in the DSSAT shell;
here every step is code that can be read, rerun and changed:

| DSSAT shell tool | Here |
|---|---|
| XBuild (experiment files) | `filex.FileX` and `filex.build_filex` from xdssat, or the file's sections edited in code |
| WeatherMan (weather files) | pandas and `wth.write_wth` / `wth.read_wth` (module 2) |
| SBuild (soil profiles) | `sol.SoilProfile`, `soils.saxton_rawls` (module 3) |
| Sensitivity Analysis tool | one FileX with a treatment per value, `learnlib.write_cultivar_variants` |
| GBuild (graphs) | the interactive charts on these pages, matplotlib in the notebooks |
| GLUE (cultivar calibration) | `glue.py`, a Python port of DSSAT's GLUE method (module 3) |
| ATCreate (observed data files) | `learnlib.write_observed` (module 4) |
| Seasonal and Sequence analysis | multi-season runs, the engine's sequence mode and pandas (modules 5 and 6) |

### The syllabus, topic by topic

Every topic of the course's six days, and where these modules cover it. "Differently" marks the topics taught
another way here, for the reasons above.

| Day | Course topic | Where | Here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | History and overview of DSSAT | [Module 1](module1.qmd), section 0 | covered |
| 1 | Running a crop model | Module 1, sections 1 and 2 | covered |
| 1 | Phenological development | Module 1, section 3 | covered |
| 1 | Potential production, creating the experiment file | Module 1, section 4 | covered |
| 1 | Sensitivity analysis | Module 1, section 5 | differently: one experiment file with a treatment per value |
| 2 | Basic growth processes | [Module 2](module2.qmd), section 1 | covered |
| 2 | Weather data and utilities, weather generators | Module 2, section 2 | differently: code in place of WeatherMan |
| 2 | Minimum data set, the DSSAT file system | Module 2, section 3 | covered |
| 2 | Species, ecotype and cultivar coefficients; cultivar sensitivity | Module 2, section 4 | covered |
| 2-3 | Estimating cultivar coefficients: concepts, GLUE, in-season data | [Module 3](module3.qmd), section 1 | differently: a Python port of GLUE |
| 3 | Soil data and utilities | Module 3, section 2 | differently: code in place of SBuild |
| 3 | Water-limited production, soil and paddy flood water | Module 3, section 3 | covered |
| 4 | Experimental data collection and files, model evaluation | [Module 4](module4.qmd), section 1 | differently: code in place of ATCreate |
| 4 | Nitrogen-limited production: soil and plant, N fixation | Module 4, section 2 | covered |
| 5 | Spatial decision support (MWCropDSS demonstration) | "From one field to a grid: xdssat", modules 1, 2, 3 and 5 | differently: xdssat in place of MWCropDSS |
| 5 | Uncertainty and risk, seasonal analysis, environmental outcomes | [Module 5](module5.qmd) | covered |
| 6 | Crop rotations, creating a sequence experiment | [Module 6](module6.qmd), sections 1 to 4 | differently: DSSAT's own sequence examples (no course material) |
| 6 | Applications and needs | Module 6, section 5 | covered |

What the DSSAT engine can do beyond the course, and which of it xdssat runs on a grid, is on
[What xdssat covers](../xdssat/coverage.qmd).

## Modules

```{ojs}
modules = [
  {n: 1, day: "1", title: "Running a crop model, phenology, sensitivity, potential production", data: "Maize UFGA8201 (Gainesville 1982)", level: "potential"},
  {n: 2, day: "2", title: "Growth processes, weather data, the DSSAT file system, cultivar coefficients", data: "Soybean UFGA7901; Griffin, Georgia weather (course data)", level: "potential"},
  {n: 3, day: "3", title: "Calibration: GLUE and in-season data; soil data; water-limited production", data: "Soybean Williams-82, peanut UFGA8401, Colorado maize and two soil sheets (course data)", level: "water-limited"},
  {n: 4, day: "4", title: "Creating crop measurement files; soil and plant nitrogen; N-limited production", data: "Peanut shading study 1976 (course data), maize UFGA8213", level: "water and N limited"},
  {n: 5, day: "5", title: "Uncertainty and risk; seasonal analysis", data: "Seasonal UFGA7812, Kadoma maize N, Niger millet (course data)", level: "over many seasons"},
  {n: 6, day: "6", title: "Cropping systems: simulating crop rotations", data: "Sequences UFGA7803 and ITHY7501", level: "over many seasons"}
].map(d => ({...d, href: `module${d.n}.qmd`, notebook: `../notebooks/module${d.n}.ipynb`}))
Inputs.table(modules, {columns: ["n", "day", "title", "data"], header: {n: "Module", day: "Training day", title: "Topics", data: "Example data"},
  format: {title: t => { const m = modules.find(d => d.title === t); return htl.html`<a href="${m.href}">${t}</a>`; }}, layout: "auto"})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 760), height: 260, marginLeft: 70,
  x: {label: "Production level the module adds", domain: ["potential", "water-limited", "water and N limited", "over many seasons"]},
  y: {label: null, domain: modules.map(d => `Module ${d.n}`)},
  marks: [Plot.cell(modules.map(d => ({m: `Module ${d.n}`, x: d.level, topics: d.title, example: d.data})),
    {x: "x", y: "m", fill: "#3f7a34", inset: 2, rx: 4, tip: true, channels: {topics: "topics", example: "example"}})]
}), "learn-dssat-modules")
```

Every module has a reading page (the links above) and a notebook in the [Notebooks](../notebooks/index.qmd)
section. The pages never run the engine: their charts read the small CSV files the notebooks wrote.

## What you need to run the notebooks

- The DSSAT engine (`dscsm048`, version 4.8), built or installed as in [Getting started](../xdssat/getting-started.md).
- A short work folder outside OneDrive (`XDSSAT_WORK`, default `C:/TEMP/dsn/work`); the engine keeps
  file paths in fixed-length buffers.
- [DSSAT/dssat-csm-data](https://github.com/DSSAT/dssat-csm-data) cloned next to the xdssat folder; the
  notebooks pin one commit.
- A Python environment with pandas, numpy and matplotlib (the one used for xdssat), and `xlrd` for the course's
  spreadsheets.
